problem_statement: Despite RAG's success in reducing hallucinations and enabling up-to-date knowledge integration, it introduces new risks—robustness issues, privacy leaks, adversarial vulnerabilities, fairness biases, lack of explainability, and accountability gaps—that threaten real-world deployment.
core_contributions: Proposes a unified six-dimensional framework (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability) for evaluating and improving trustworthiness in RAG systems
Introduces structured taxonomies and evaluation protocols for each trustworthiness dimension, enabling systematic comparison of methods
Identifies critical open challenges and synergistic research directions across trustworthiness dimensions, serving as a community roadmap
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on trustworthiness dimensions of RAG; does not propose novel algorithms or datasets, but synthesizes and structures existing work.

evidence_spans.claim_value: six-dimensional framework (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability)
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We place our discussion around five key perspectives: reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, and accountability.

For each perspective, we present a general framework and taxonomy, offering a structured approach to understanding the current challenges, evaluating existing solutions, and identifying promising future research directions.
This survey not only serves as a comprehensive roadmap for researchers aiming to advance trustworthy RAG systems...

problem_statement: Conventional RAG fails to capture complex inter-knowledge relationships; GraphRAG suffers from graph noise and incompleteness.
core_contributions: Introduces GFM-RAG, the first graph foundation model for RAG that generalizes to unseen datasets without fine-tuning
Proposes a novel graph neural network architecture that explicitly reasons over graph structure to model query-knowledge relationships
Trains an 8M-parameter GFM on large-scale heterogeneous data (60 KGs, 14M triples, 700k documents), enabling strong zero-shot retrieval
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on graph-structured knowledge integration in RAG; does not address multimodal or temporal graph extensions.

evidence_spans.claim_value: GFM-RAG is the first graph foundation model applicable to unseen datasets for retrieval without any fine-tuning required
evidence_spans.evidence_text: making it the first graph foundation model applicable to unseen datasets for retrieval without any fine-tuning required

evidence_spans.claim_value: GFM-RAG is powered by an innovative graph neural network that reasons over graph structure
evidence_spans.evidence_text: GFM-RAG is powered by an innovative graph neural network that reasons over graph structure to capture complex query-knowledge relationships

evidence_spans.claim_value: Trained on 60 knowledge graphs with over 14M triples and 700k documents
evidence_spans.evidence_text: comprising 60 knowledge graphs with over 14M triples and 700k documents

problem_statement: Semantic-only RAG retrieves isolated, redundant chunks lacking intrinsic relationships, limiting LLM reasoning and response coherence.
core_contributions: Introduces KG2RAG: a novel RAG framework that leverages knowledge graphs to model fact-level relationships among retrieved chunks.
Proposes KG-guided chunk expansion to diversify and enrich retrieval results beyond semantic similarity.
Designs KG-based context organization to structure retrieved chunks into coherent, paragraph-level inputs for LLMs.
limitations_or_scope: Limited to structured KG construction from Wikipedia-style documents; manual prompting used for triplet extraction; long-tail distribution of KG triplets per chunk may affect coverage.

evidence_spans.claim_value: KG2RAG uses knowledge graphs to provide fact-level relationships between chunks
evidence_spans.evidence_text: utilizes knowledge graphs (KGs) to provide fact-level relationships between chunks

evidence_spans.claim_value: KG-guided chunk expansion improves diversity and coherence of retrieved results
evidence_spans.evidence_text: KG2RAG employs a KG-guided chunk expansion process and a KG-based chunk organization process to deliver relevant and important knowledge in well-organized paragraphs
We conduct experiments on the benchmark dataset HotpotQA Yang et al. (2018)... HotpotQA-Dist and HotpotQA-Full

problem_statement: LLMs struggle with robust multi-hop reasoning over very long contexts—even with large context windows—due to scattered evidence and lack of explicit retrieval-integration mechanisms.
model_tags: LLMs with long context support (e.g., >100k tokens)
core_contributions: Proposes a single-pass prompt engineering method that emulates RAG by combining relevance tagging and chain-of-thought reasoning within one LLM call.
Demonstrates improved accuracy on multi-fact QA tasks (e.g., object tracking, counting, indefinite knowledge) in long-context settings using BABILong.
Identifies critical prompt structure effects—especially instruction/question/context ordering—on long-context comprehension performance.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on synthetic long-context QA (BABILong); does not address real-world retrieval or domain-specific corpora; assumes model supports very long context windows.

evidence_spans.claim_value: emulates RAG via prompt engineering and chain-of-thought reasoning
evidence_spans.evidence_text: This paper addresses the challenge of comprehending very long contexts in Large Language Models (LLMs) by proposing a method that emulates Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) through specialized prompt engineering and chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning.

evidence_spans.claim_value: evaluated on BABILong with distractor text and up to 64k tokens
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We evaluate on BABILong (Kuratov et al., 2024), a long-context QA benchmark derived from the classic bAbI tasks. The dataset interleaves large amounts of distractor text (PG19) with relevant question-answer pairs, creating contexts of up to tens of thousands of tokens.
These findings underscore that optimized prompt engineering, combined with guided reasoning, can enhance LLMs’ long-context comprehension...

problem_statement: Fragmented tooling and lack of standardized, flexible frameworks hinder consistent comparison and benchmarking of retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG methods.
core_contributions: Introduces Rankify, a unified open-source Python toolkit for retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG
Provides modular support for diverse retrievers (sparse/dense/hybrid), state-of-the-art re-rankers, and RAG pipelines
Includes pre-retrieved benchmark datasets and built-in evaluation metrics (Top-k accuracy, EM, recall, precision, containment)
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on modularity and ease of use; does not introduce novel retrieval/re-ranking algorithms or theoretical advances.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Rankify is a unified open-source Python toolkit for retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG
evidence_spans.evidence_text: we introduce Rankify, a powerful and modular open-source toolkit designed to unify retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG within a cohesive framework

evidence_spans.claim_value: Supports sparse, dense, and hybrid retrievers and state-of-the-art re-rankers
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Rankify supports a wide range of retrieval techniques, including dense and sparse retrievers, while incorporating state-of-the-art re-ranking models

evidence_spans.claim_value: Includes pre-retrieved datasets and built-in evaluation metrics
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Rankify includes a collection of pre-retrieved datasets to facilitate benchmarking... Rankify provides evaluation metrics for retrieval, re-ranking, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
